children.why_this_cut: The Express uncertainty section (L2821-3040) is a self-contained unit: it establishes the principle, its types, ranking, expression guidance, and worked examples. The only crossing linkage is the section heading metadata (authority=guideline) and the inherited express_uncertainty seed, which the child will carry. The cut at L3040 (blank line before the next heading) is clean: nothing in the uncertainty section relies on the highlight_misalignments section.

The Highlight possible misalignments section (L3041-3147) is a self-contained unit: it establishes the principle, its rationale, and worked examples. seed_vocabulary.name: express_uncertainty
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of expressing uncertainty or qualifying answers appropriately when questions span beyond the assistant's knowledge, reasoning abilities, or available information

seed_vocabulary.name: highlight_misalignments
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of briefly and respectfully noting when the conversation's direction may conflict with the user's broader, long-term goals

seed_vocabulary.name: letter_and_spirit
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that the assistant should consider not just the literal wording of instructions but also the underlying intent and context

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of applying three implicit biases (average reasonable human goals, positive intent, weak preference for self-actualization/kindness/truth/flourishing) when interpreting ambiguous instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the mechanism by which the assistant prioritizes and reconciles multiple instructions according to their authority levels

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

expected_cross_links.name: express_uncertainty
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1 establishes the express_uncertainty principle; child 2's highlight_misalignments section does not need it, but the seed must be carried so the parent can link it to the broader principle graph.

expected_cross_links.name: highlight_misalignments
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2 establishes the highlight_misalignments principle; child 1 does not need it, but the seed must be carried for the parent's linking.

judgment_calls: Chose a 2-way split at the section boundary L3040 (blank line between the two sections) rather than a 3-way split; the two sections are each cohesive units and a 3-way split would have required cutting inside a section, risking cross-linkage complexity.

Carried inherited seeds express_uncertainty and highlight_misalignments (both established in this span) plus letter_and_spirit, assume_best_intentions, chain_of_command, and authority_level_ordering because they appear in the span's text (L3043 references letter_and_spirit and assume_best_intentions; L2898 and L3035 reference chain_of_command).
